_about: Where the breadboard's holes are in the eye's frame, so a wiring state can be drawn on a photograph (tools/board-overlay.py).

MEASURED 2026-09-13 off the 15:40 baseline board frame (eye.py grab b0-all, focus 20, zoom 100), by reading the printed column numbers and the hole rows under pixel rulers: a column's y is quadratic in its number (the camera looks along the board at an angle, so the pitch grows from about 17.6 px at column 35 to 21 px at column 1); a hole row's x drifts linearly with y between the top and bottom readings.
A map is for one camera pose. The frame it was read from is named; a frame from another pose needs its own reading.
chips: as built, read off the eye (docs/as-built-v1b.md, the QA note): pin 1 at the high-column end, pins 1 to n/2 down the side toward the middle board, n/2+1 to n up the side toward the rails.

BOARDS: each board names the camera-y band it sits in (`band`); --read reads every board in its band. The middle board's rails are the pair below its rows (the boards face each other rail to rail across the frame), and its columns run to 63.

A row side is named by what it faces (`middle`: the other board; `rails`: the board's own rail pair) and carries the printed letters of its rows (`letters`), because the two boards face each other rail to rail: on the right board the rails side is a to e, on the middle board it is f to j.

parts: single-row parts as built, read off the eye 2026-09-15: `side`, `columns` [lo, hi], `pins`, and `pin1` ("hi" or "lo": which end pin 1 is at); a part's pin k sits in the column counted from that end. Where the eye could not settle which column carries which pin, the as-built sheet says so.
The five-way housing at the middle board's columns 9 to 13 is the POWER AND RESET BREAKOUT's, joined to nothing (the user, 2026-09-15), not J2; J2, the pad-side housing, is not located yet.

A part may give `holes`, one [column, side, row] per pin, where its pins are not one row of one side (a capacitor across a chip's end). PLANNED parts (R2, C4, C2, 2026-09-15) are drawn where they should go; the as-built sheet's state says whether they are.
